title: Release State v1
description: The whole content of specs/releases/<release-id>/_RELEASE.json — ONE mutable JSON object, the release's current state, never an append-only event stream (operator ruling: 'e um arquivo altamente mutavel onde acompanhamos o estado do release. Nao faz sentido ser append-only' — retires release-event-v1.schema.json and its _RELEASE.jsonl fold, core/release_events.py). `phase`, `rc`, `defined`, `implemented` and `shipped` are rewritten IN PLACE through core/atomic_write.py's compare-and-swap seam (expected_previous, refuse-stale) whenever a code path writes this document; an agent with file tools (product-engineer, at the phase boundaries this document's history used to record as separate `phase` lines) may also Read-then-Edit it directly, the same discipline a CAS write enforces mechanically. `defined`/`implemented`/`shipped` are the three sha-bearing milestone facts (each set at most once meaningfully — a later legitimate rewrite is a correction, not a second append, so there is no more 'duplicate milestone' finding to detect: SPEC-DOC-043 retires with the JSONL fold it existed to police). An audit is NOT a release milestone: the audit window is read from audits/_archive/audits_histo.jsonl (0.4.7 FR7), so the fourth `audited` milestone is deleted rather than left as a field no code path ever wrote. `log` is the one place free-form governance narrative survives INSIDE this otherwise-typed document — the closure narrative that _RELEASE.jsonl's `note` records used to carry, one entry per note, oldest first, never rewritten once appended, each classified by the closed `kind` enum.

schema.description: This schema's own id, carried in every document for a self-describing file.

release.description: Bare SemVer release id (e.g. '0.6.0') — matches the directory name this file lives under.

phase.description: The release's current lifecycle phase. The four canonical phases are enumerated here AND in core/release_state.py (PHASES) — the two are pinned equal by tests/contract/test_release_state_schema.py, so neither can drift. Overwritten in place on every phase transition — no history of prior phases survives in this field; a transition worth remembering is recorded as a `log` entry.

rc.description: The current/most recent rc round number, or null before any rc round has opened.

defined.description: Set once, at the definition promotion commit (project-manager). null before that point.

sha.description: The final-rc QA-close commit sha — not the merge commit (the two differ by the merge artifact).

rc.description: Which rc round closed this milestone.

implemented.description: Set once, at the final-rc close (code-reviewer). null before that point.

shipped.description: Set once, at the develop->main ship merge. null before that point.

log.description: Append-only governance narrative living inside this mutable document, oldest first. An entry is appended, never edited or removed once written.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp this note was appended.

agent.description: Agent or runtime that appended this note.

kind.description: The closure-narrative category of this log entry, from the closed enum below: 'note' (anything with no dedicated kind) plus the nine narrative kinds a candidate closure writes — summary, size, drifts, dispositions, test-dispositions, artifact-gc, reviews, merge, memory.
